title: Arakhin 34
description: The last daf of Arakhin: why a Levite city whose walls stand to be dismantled still needs its own rule of perpetual redemption, and why a priest who consecrates a field he received as a dedication cannot keep it at the Jubilee, ending with the hadran on the chapter and the tractate.
topics: 🏘️ The cities of the Levites and their open land: walled cities that stand to be dismantled
🧱 Rav Ashi: until the walls come down, might a house sold there be lost for good?
📜 “As a field dedicated”: a priest who consecrates his own dedicated field
⚖️ “I acquire the fields of others; my own, all the more so?” Merely acquiring is not taking
🍖 Rami bar Ḥama: “every man’s hallowed things shall be his”, and why that is not comparable
🌾 Rav Naḥman: “his ancestral field”, yes; his dedicated field, no
🎉 Hadran: the end of HaMokher Sadehu and of Masechet Arakhin
attribution: English: William Davidson Edition - English (CC-BY-NC). Aramaic: William Davidson Edition - Vocalized Aramaic (CC-BY-NC). Commentaries: Sefaria (Vilna edition), English renderings by WhatsDaf.

a1.he: הֵן וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶן, הֵן וּמִגְרְשֵׁיהֶן לְמִיסְתְּרִינְהוּ קָיְימִי. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: אַדְּמִסְתַּתְּרִי מִסְתַּתְּרִי, אִי מִיזְדַּבְּנִי לִיחַלְטוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a2.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? מִנַּיִן לְכֹהֵן שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שְׂדֵה חֶרְמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר: הוֹאִיל וְיוֹצָא לַכֹּהֲנִים, וַהֲרֵי הִיא תַּחַת יָדִי — תְּהֵא שֶׁלִּי.

a3.he: וְדִין הוּא: בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים אֲנִי זוֹכֶה, בְּשֶׁל עַצְמִי לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קוֹדֶשׁ לַה׳ כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם״.

a4.he: וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִשְּׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם מֵעַתָּה? הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד, מַקִּישׁ שְׂדֵה חֶרְמוֹ לִשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל: מָה שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצָא מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לַכֹּהֲנִים, אַף שְׂדֵה חֶרְמוֹ יוֹצָא מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ וּמִתְחַלֶּקֶת לְאֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים.

a5.he: אָמַר מָר: בְּשֶׁל אֲחֵרִים אֲנִי זוֹכֶה. מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם זוֹכֶה בְּעָלְמָא, הָכָא קָא שָׁקֵיל לֵיהּ.

a6.he: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״וְאִישׁ אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו לוֹ יִהְיוּ״, הָא נָמֵי כִּי קֳדָשָׁיו דָּמְיָא.

a7.he: מִי דָּמֵי? קֳדָשָׁיו לָאו בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, הָכָא בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ.

a8.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״כִּי אֲחוּזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם״, הָא נָמֵי אֲחוּזָּתוֹ הִיא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן ״אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״ — אֲחוּזָּתוֹ אִין, חֶרְמוֹ לָא.

a9.he: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ, וּסְלִיקָא לָהּ מַסֶּכֶת עֲרָכִין.

messages.text: Continued from 33b: the Gemara asked how a baraita can speak of Levite houses in walled cities when Levite cities may not be surrounded by a wall. Rav Yosef, son of Rav Sala Ḥasida, interpreted the baraita before Rav Pappa: it speaks of a case where, when the land was divided, walled cities fell by lottery to the Levites,
both they and their empty lots.

notes.he: כשהן מוקפות חומה:
notes.en: They and their lots: when they are surrounded by a wall.

notes.he: כלומר עם חומותיהן:
notes.en: They and their lots: that is, together with their walls.

messages.text: But they and their lots stand to be dismantled, as a city of the Levites may not be surrounded by a wall. How, then, can such a city be considered surrounded by a wall?

notes.he: כדאמר (לעיל ערכין דף לג:) אין עושין אותן טירין וכרכים:
notes.en: But they stand to be dismantled: as was said (above, Arakhin 33b): one does not make them into small villages or large cities.

notes.he: וא"ת מאי נפקא מינה אם נסתרו כיון שהיו מוקפות חומה מעיקרא דהא תניא לעיל אשר לו חומה ואע"פ שאין לו עכשיו והיה לו קודם לכן ושמא י"ל דאתיא כרבי אלעזר בר' יוסי ושאני הכא כיון שהם ראויות שלא יהא להם חומה לא תועיל להם קדושת חומה שהיה קודם לכן כאילו לא היתה מעולם:
notes.en: They and their lots stand to be dismantled: And if you ask, what difference does it make if they were dismantled, since they were surrounded by a wall originally? For it was taught above: “that has a wall” — even though it does not have one now, as long as it had one before. Perhaps one can say that this follows Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei. And here it is different: since they are fit not to have a wall, the sanctity of the wall that they had before does not help them, and it is as if it had never been.

notes.he: כלומר הא עומדין ליסתור חומתן שהרי אין עושין אותן לא טירין ולא כרכין ואכתי לית להו בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: And their lots stand to be dismantled: that is, but their walls stand to be dismantled, since one does not make them into either small villages or large cities, and so they still do not have [the status of] houses of walled cities.

messages.text: Nevertheless, it was necessary for the baraita to teach that if a Levite sells a house in such a city he may always redeem it, as it might enter your mind to say: When the walls are dismantled, then they are dismantled, but as long as they remain standing, if houses in the city are sold and are not redeemed within one year, let them belong to the buyer in perpetuity, in accordance with the halakha of houses of walled cities. Therefore, the baraita teaches us that this is not the case.
messages.quote: they and their lots stand to be dismantled

notes.he: כל זמן שלא נסתרו אם מכרום קודם סתירתן ליחלטו קמ"ל:
notes.en: It might enter your mind: as long as they have not been dismantled, if they sold them before they were dismantled, let them become the buyer’s permanently. It teaches us [that this is not so].

notes.dh: [אפילו הכי איצטריך גאולת עולם סד"א אדמיסתתרי איסתורי
notes.he: כלומר מקמי דליסתרי אי מיזדבני ליחלטו קמ"ל גאולת עולם:
notes.en: Even so, perpetual redemption was necessary. It might enter your mind: before they are dismantled… that is, before they are dismantled, if they are sold, let them become [the buyer’s] permanently. It teaches us perpetual redemption.

messages.text: The verse states, with regard to one who consecrated his ancestral field but failed to redeem it before the Jubilee Year: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy unto the Lord, as a field dedicated; his ancestral field shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). What is the meaning when the verse states: “As a field dedicated”?

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: כשדה החרם מה בא שדה החרם ללמד על שדה היוצאת לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: What does the verse teach: “as a field dedicated”: what does the dedicated field come to teach about a field that goes out to the priests in the Jubilee?

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to a priest who consecrated his dedicated field, i.e., a field that was dedicated to the priests by an Israelite, and the Jubilee Year arrived, that he may not say: Since a field that was consecrated by its owners and was not redeemed leaves to the possession of the priests in the Jubilee Year, and this field that I consecrated is already in my possession, it is therefore mine.

notes.he: שדה שהחרים ישראל והגיעה לחלקו:
notes.en: His dedicated field: a field that an Israelite dedicated and that came into his share.

notes.he: אם לא יגאלנה שהרי היא שלו כשדה אחוזה ועכשיו הרי היא תחת ידי כו':
notes.en: Since it goes out to the priests: if he does not redeem it, for it is his like an ancestral field; and now it is in my possession, etc.

notes.he: שהחרימה ישראל ובאתה ליד כהן והקדישה ולא הספיק לגאלה עד שפגע בו יובל:
notes.en: His dedicated field: which an Israelite dedicated and which came into the hand of a priest, and he consecrated it and did not manage to redeem it before the Jubilee arrived.

notes.dh: שלא יאמר הואיל ויוצאה לכהנים ביובל
notes.he: דהאי כהן שמקדיש שדה חרמו הוי כאילו הקדיש שדה אחוזתו ולא גאלה שיוצאה לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: That he may not say: since it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee — for this priest who consecrates his dedicated field is as though he consecrated his ancestral field and did not redeem it, which goes out to the priests in the Jubilee.

messages.text: And this is the halakha despite the fact that the claim of the priest is based on logical inference: If I acquire the fields of others that were consecrated and not redeemed before the Jubilee Year, then with regard to my own property, should I not all the more so acquire it?

notes.he: אם היה שדה אחוזת ישראל יוצאה לכהנים ביובל היה לי חלק בה:
notes.en: I acquire those of others: if an Israelite’s ancestral field were going out to the priests in the Jubilee, I would have a share in it.

notes.he: שדה שהקדישה ישראל ולא גאלה שיוצאה לכהנים אני זוכה בה:
notes.en: Those of others: a field that an Israelite consecrated and did not redeem, which goes out to the priests — I acquire it.

notes.he: שאזכה בה שלא תצא מתחת ידי:
notes.en: My own, all the more so: that I should acquire it, so that it does not leave my possession.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “As a field dedicated, his ancestral field shall be for the priest,” which teaches that this is not the case.

But what have we learned about a consecrated ancestral field from a dedicated field from now? The Torah does not explicitly state the halakha with regard to dedicated fields. Rather, this case of a dedicated field came to teach a halakha with regard to an ancestral field, and it turns out that in addition it derives a halakha from that case,

i.e., the verse juxtaposes the dedicated field of a priest to the ancestral field of an Israelite: Just as the ancestral field of an Israelite that was redeemed by a priest from the Temple treasury leaves from his possession at the arrival of the Jubilee Year and is divided among all the priests (see 25a), so too, the dedicated field of a priest that he consecrated leaves from his possession and is divided among his brothers, the priests, at the beginning of the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: אם גאלה כהן מיד הקדש יוצאה מידו ביובל ומתחלקת לכל אחיו הכהנים כדאמר באידך פירקא בפרק אין מקדישין (לעיל ערכין דף כה:) אף זו כו':
notes.en: Just as the ancestral field of an Israelite: if a priest redeemed it from the Temple treasury, it goes out of his possession in the Jubilee and is divided among all his brothers the priests, as was said in the other chapter, the chapter Ein Makdishin (above, Arakhin 25b). So too this one, etc.

notes.he: שהקדישה ישראל ולא גאלה שיוצאה מיד הקדש לכהנים ביובל וגאלה אחד מן הכהנים יוצאה מידו ומתחלקת לכל אחיו הכהנים כדאמר לעיל בפרק המקדיש שדהו שאחוזתו שלו ואין זו שלו אלא של כל הכהנים:
notes.en: Just as the ancestral field of an Israelite: which an Israelite consecrated and did not redeem, which goes out from the Temple treasury to the priests in the Jubilee; and if one of the priests redeemed it, it goes out of his possession and is divided among all his brothers the priests, as was said above in the chapter HaMakdish Sadehu: his ancestral field is his, but this one is not his; it belongs to all the priests.

notes.he: ומתחלקת לכל אחיו הכהנים]:
notes.en: So too his dedicated field goes out and is divided among all his brothers the priests.

messages.text: And this claim of the priest is based on logical inference: If I acquire the fields of others that were consecrated, then with regard to my own property, should I not acquire it all the more so?
messages.lead: The Gemara analyzes this baraita: The Master said:
messages.quote: If I acquire the fields of others

messages.text: Are these cases comparable? There, with regard to an ancestral field that was consecrated and leaves to the possession of the priests, he merely acquires it as one of the priests, whereas here, with regard to a dedicated field that he consecrated, he seeks to take the entire field for himself. If so, there is no need for the verse to teach that the priest may not do so.

notes.he: הכא קא שקיל ליה כו':
notes.en: Here he takes it, etc. [Rashi gives only the heading.]

notes.he: והכא נמי הוי מצי למיפרך כשהוא זוכה בשל אחרים והוי במשמר שלו אבל הכא רצה לזכות משמר אחר והיא אינה מתחלקת לכהנים של משמר אחר כדפי' לעיל (ערכין דף כה.) אלא דעדיפא מינה פריך שאפילו באה משמרתו כשיוצאה לכהנים אין לזכות מהאי קל וחומר:
notes.en: Are they comparable? There he acquires: Here too [the Gemara] could have objected that when he acquires the fields of others, it is when it falls during his own priestly watch, whereas here he wants to acquire it [even] for another watch, and it is not divided among the priests of another watch, as explained above (Arakhin 25a). But it raises a stronger objection than that: even if his own watch is serving when it goes out to the priests, he cannot acquire it [all for himself] by this a fortiori inference.

notes.he: קא זכי בעלמא. דרחמנא זכי ליה שדה אחוזה של ישראל היוצאה לכהנים עם שאר הכהנים:
notes.en: Are they comparable? There he merely acquires: for the Merciful One grants him [a share in] the ancestral field of an Israelite that goes out to the priests, together with the other priests.

notes.he: כלומר ממי זכה שיתפוס שדה חרמו לעצמו:
notes.en: Here he takes all of it: that is, from whom did he gain [the right] to seize his dedicated field for himself?

messages.text: Nevertheless, the verse was necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that since it is written: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his” (Numbers 5:10), from which it is derived that a priest who brings an offering may sacrifice it and take for himself those portions intended for the priests and he is not required to give them to the members of the current priestly watch, perhaps this too, i.e., his dedicated field that he consecrated, is considered like his hallowed things, and he may take it for himself. Therefore, the verse serves to indicate that this is not the case.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֶת־קֳדָשָׁיו לוֹ יִהְיוּ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִתֵּן לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה׃ {פ}
verse.en: And each shall retain his sacred donations: each priest shall keep what is given to him.

notes.he: ודרשינן ליה בהגוזל בב"ק (דף קט:) מנין לכהן שבא ומקריב קרבנותיו בכל עת ובכל שעה שירצה אם יש עליו להביא חטאת או התנדב עולה או שלמים אין צריך לתתם לאנשי משמר אלא הוא עצמו מקריב ויטול העור ואוכל הבשר ת"ל ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו:
notes.en: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his”: we expound this in the chapter HaGozel in Bava Kamma (109b): From where do we know that a priest may come and offer his offerings at any time and any hour he wishes — if he must bring a sin offering, or he volunteered a burnt offering or a peace offering — and he need not give them to the men of the priestly watch, but he himself offers it, takes the hide and eats the meat? The verse states: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his.”

notes.dh: אמר רמי בר חמא איצטריך כו' [אלא] אמר רב נחמן [איצטריך] ס"ד כו'
notes.he: ואם תאמר מאי היא דנאמר ודין הוא והלא אין לנו לומר שזוכה בו מטעם קל וחומר אלא מטעם דכתיבי קראי דאיש כי יקדיש לרמי בר חמא ולאחוזת עולם לרב נחמן וי"ל דמכל מקום ניחא ליה לאיתויי קל וחומר כך מסברא:
notes.en: Rami bar Ḥama said: It was necessary, etc. [Rather,] Rav Naḥman said: [It was necessary;] it might enter your mind, etc. And if you ask: what is it that we said, “and it is a logical inference”? We should not be saying that he acquires it by an a fortiori inference, but because of the verses written: “a man…” [Tosafot’s text reads “when a man consecrates”; the verse Rami bar Ḥama cites is “And every man’s hallowed things”] for Rami bar Ḥama, and “perpetual possession” for Rav Naḥman. One can say: nevertheless, [the baraita] preferred to bring an a fortiori inference like this, from reasoning.

notes.he: אכתי איצטריך דסד"א דהאי ודין הוא דינא הוי הואיל וכתיב ואיש את קדשיו לו יהיו [ומפרש בסיפרי מנין לישראל שהיה מודד תרומה לכהן ע"ג קרקע מנין שכל כהן שיבא שם באותה שעה שהוא מודד שיש לו חלק בהן כמו זה הראשון ת"ל איש את קדשיו לו יהיו] כלומר לכולן בשוה יכול אפילו מדד לו לתוך קופתו של ראשון שיזכה אחר [עמו] ת"ל אשר יתן לכהן לו יהיה ולא לאחר סד"א כי היכי דזוכה בקדשים שנוטל חלקו עם כהן ראשון אם בא עד שלא מדד לו שאינו יכול לדחותו [והאי שדה חרמו כי קדשיו דמי ולא יהא אדם יכול לדחותו אלא תהא שלו להכי איצטריך היקישא]:
notes.en: Rami bar Ḥama said: It was still necessary, for it might enter your mind that this “and it is a logical inference” is a real inference, since it is written: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his.” [It is explained in the Sifrei: From where do we know, of an Israelite who was measuring out teruma for a priest on the ground, that any priest who comes there while he is measuring has a share in it like this first one? The verse states: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his”,] that is, for all of them equally. One might think that even if he had measured it into the basket of the first one, another would acquire [with him]? The verse states: “whatever any man gives the priest, it shall be his” — and not another’s. So it might enter your mind that just as he acquires in sacred things, taking his share with the first priest if he came before it was measured out to him, so that the first one cannot push him away, [so too this dedicated field is like his hallowed things, and no one can push him away, but it should be his. That is why the juxtaposition was necessary.]

messages.text: Are these cases comparable? His hallowed things, i.e., offerings brought by the priest, are not in his possession; rather, the priest receives the priestly portions from the table of the Most High, in exchange for performing the sacrificial rites. Here, the priest seeks to return the field to his possession.
messages.quote: is considered like his hallowed things

notes.he: ולאו מכח דידיה קא שקיל להו אלא מקריב אימוריהם:
notes.en: His hallowed things are not in his possession: and he does not take them by his own right, but because he offers their sacrificial portions.

notes.he: כלומר מכח דידיה קא שקיל להו ולא משלחן גבוה בשכר עבודה:
notes.en: Here it is in his possession: that is, he would take it by his own right, and not from the table of the Most High as wages for the service.

notes.he: האי קדשים לחרמי קדשים. קדשים לאו ברשותו נינהו אלא ברשות ישראל נינהו [בעלמא] קא זכי ליה רחמנא הכא האי שדה חרמו ברשותו הוא [וברשותו] מאן זכי ליה ולאו דינא הוא:
notes.en: Are they comparable — these hallowed things to the dedicated field? Hallowed things are not in his possession but in the Israelite’s possession; the Merciful One [merely] grants them to him. Here, this dedicated field is in his own possession; [and while it is in his possession,] who grants it to him? It is not a valid inference.

messages.text: The verse was necessary, as it might enter your mind to say that since it is written with regard to the fields of Levites and priests: “For that is their perpetual possession” (Leviticus 25:34), from which it is derived that if a priest consecrated his ancestral field he may always redeem it, so too this dedicated field received by the priest is also considered his ancestral field, and if he consecrated it he may always redeem it.

verse.he: וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר כִּי־אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: But the unenclosed land about its cities cannot be sold, for that is its holding for all time.

notes.he: להכי איצטריך למכתב החרם דסד"א כו' והאי נמי אחוזתו היא ואם הקדישה ולא גאלה לא תצא לכהנים ביובל אלא יהא לו רשות לגאלה לעולם:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Naḥman said: this is why it was necessary to write “dedicated”, for it might enter your mind, etc., that this too is his ancestral field, and if he consecrated it and did not redeem it, it would not go out to the priests in the Jubilee; rather, he would have the right to redeem it forever.

notes.dh: איצטריך סד"א הואיל וכתיב כי אחוזת עולם היא להם
notes.he: דהדרא ליה ביובל ואינה יוצאה מידו האי נמי שדה חרמו אחוזתו היא ולא תצא מתחת ידו להכי איצטריך היקישא דאחוזתו היא שלו אבל שדה חרמו לא אלא תצא מתחת ידו ותתחלקת לאחיו הכהנים. לשון מורי הגאון. קדשיו לאו ברשותו דמוקי ליה להאי קרא בגזל הגר ומת שמשלם קרן וחומש לכהנים [ואשם למזבח]:
notes.en: It was necessary; it might enter your mind: since it is written “for that is their perpetual possession” — that it returns to him in the Jubilee and does not leave his possession — this dedicated field too is his ancestral field and should not leave his possession. That is why the juxtaposition was necessary: his ancestral field is his, but his dedicated field is not; rather, it leaves his possession and is divided among his brothers the priests. [This is] the wording of my teacher the Gaon. “His hallowed things are not in his possession”: [a note in the printed edition adds:] See Bava Kamma 109, which implies that it speaks of a priest who comes to offer his offerings in a watch that is not his, and nevertheless its service and its hide are his; see there. Perhaps it means that since this verse is adjacent to the verse about robbing a convert, we expound the adjacency, so that this verse too speaks of robbing a convert: for example, a priest who robbed a convert may offer the guilt offering in another watch, and its service and its hide are his. For it establishes this verse as referring to robbing a convert who died, where he pays the principal and the fifth to the priests [and the guilt offering goes to the altar].

messages.text: The juxtaposition of the dedicated field of a priest to the ancestral field of an Israelite teaches us that this is not the halakha, as the verse states: “His ancestral field shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). The verse teaches that with regard to the ancestral field of a priest that he inherited from his father, yes, it remains in the possession of that priest in perpetuity, but with regard to his dedicated field, it does not remain in his possession in perpetuity; rather, it is divided among the members of the priestly watch serving at the beginning of the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: היקש דאיתקש שדה החרם לשדה אחוזתו של ישראל דתצא מתחת ידו ותתחלק לכהנים דאחוזתו היא דיש לה גאולת עולם אבל חרמו לא הויא כאחוזה ליגאל לעולם:
notes.en: It teaches us: the juxtaposition, by which the dedicated field is juxtaposed to the ancestral field of an Israelite, [teaches] that it goes out of his possession and is divided among the priests. For it is his ancestral field that has redemption forever, but his dedicated field is not like an ancestral field, to be redeemed forever.

notes.dh: הא קא משמע לן אחוזתו אחוזתו אין חרמו לא
notes.he: ואם תאמר הא לעיל ילפינן מהקישא דמקיש שדה חרמו לשדה אחוזה לישראל ואמאי דריש ליה הכא מאחוזתו ויש לומר דהכי פירושו קא משמע לן מאחוזתו של כהן דאחוזתו דוקא יש לה גאולת עולם ואינה מתחלקת לכהנים ביובל אבל שדה חרמו מתחלק לכהנים ביובל מהיקשא דמקשינן ליה לשדה אחוזה של ישראל ולא הויא כשדה אחוזתו ליגאל לעולם וכן פרש"י:
notes.en: It teaches us “his ancestral field”: his ancestral field, yes; his dedicated field, no. And if you ask: above we derived it from the juxtaposition, which juxtaposes his dedicated field to the ancestral field of an Israelite, so why does it expound it here from “his ancestral field”? One can say that this is its meaning: it teaches us from “the ancestral field” of the priest that specifically his ancestral field has redemption forever and is not divided among the priests in the Jubilee, but his dedicated field is divided among the priests in the Jubilee, by the juxtaposition that juxtaposes it to the ancestral field of an Israelite, and it is not like his ancestral field, to be redeemed forever. And so Rashi explained.
